reports.title: Patryk Gladysz: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

promises.quote: Staffing within the Mental Health In-reach team
promises.summary: Recruitment and retention of substantive staff remains a priority; permanent fill rate now 81% and vacancies being recruited with anticipated start

concerns.quote: Staffing within the Mental Health In-reach team impacting the timely undertaking of meaningful and quality mental health assessments
concerns.hazard: delayed or inadequate mental health assessments

concerns.quote: Staffing within HMP Wandsworth resulting in a dilution to the requirements for the key worker scheme
concerns.hazard: insufficient staffing affecting key worker responsibilities

concerns.quote: Knowledge of prison staff of the heightened risk of foreign nationals in custody, despite a higher proportion of foreign nationals being detained at HMP Wandsworth
concerns.hazard: lack of awareness of heightened risk to foreign nationals

concerns.quote: Communication between prison and healthcare staff regarding: (a) knowledge sharing of those presenting with a serious and enduring mental health illness, such as schizophrenia; (b) inconsistent understanding of healthcare access to the NOMIS by both prison and healthcare staff; and (c) de-activation of NOMIS accounts for healthcare staff due to lack of use - 21 healthcare accounts were de-activated notwithstanding an increase in available terminals
concerns.hazard: poor communication and inconsistent NOMIS account management

concerns.quote: Prison officer checks of roll calls/ACCT observations - recent audit by HMP Wandsworth suggests on-going challenges
concerns.hazard: inadequate roll call and ACCT observations

concerns.quote: First Aid refresher training is not up to date for all healthcare staff
concerns.hazard: outdated first aid training among healthcare staff

reports.title: Thomas Ruggiero (2): Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: There is a policy requirement / expectation that a member of the healthcare team should attend all ACCT reviews. In this case, there were numerous instances that this was not met. While I heard evidence of some improvement, it was accepted that there were ongoing issues with securing the attendance of the mental health team (where required) at ACCT reviews. I was insufficiently reassured that the matter has been addressed and I consider that there is ongoing risk to particularly vulnerable prisoners for whom the ACCT processes should act as a safety-net and protective factor.
concerns.hazard: lack of mental health team attendance at ACCT reviews

links.explanation: Both reports highlight problems with ensuring mental health staff are adequately involved in prison care processes. The earlier report cites staffing shortages affecting mental health assessments, while the later report notes failures to meet the policy requirement for mental health team attendance at ACCT reviews.
